This study presents a comprehensive first-principles investigation into the structural, electrical, magnetic, mechanical, optical, and thermodynamic properties of two lithium-based half-Heusler semiconductors, LiSiIn and LiSnAl.

Phonon dispersion confirms dynamic stability, and thermodynamic results show low minimum thermal conductivities (similar to 0.006-0.007 W m-1 K-1) and high melting points (1003.46 K for LiSnAl, 1100.02 K for LiSiIn).
The higher melting point of LiSiIn reflects stronger bonding, while LiSnAl's lower thermal conductivity favors thermal energy storage.
